title_zh: 大家已经同意了，还能继续追问吗？
title_en: An Agreement Is Not the End of Questions
deck_zh: 出生证上的“未定”、没有结算的收据、被抽到不同去处的一家人。谁能把这些事问到作决定的地方，谁又不能独自宣布已经答完？
deck_en: An unsettled nationality, an unpaid receipt, a family assigned to different destinations. Who can bring these questions to the decision-maker—and who gets to say the answer is enough?
body_zh: 孩子出生了，出生证上国籍一栏写着“未定”。等到下一年，那两个字还在那里。
在原论文的虚构故事里，这不是一张证件的疏漏。战争期间，DRP，也就是目的民主共和国，规定出境六个月不归的人丧失国籍；他们在境外出生的孩子，不予登记。收留他们的邻国，也有自己的门槛。大人跨过边界以后，孩子便出生在两套制度之间。
后来，三国结成协作体系，DRP 接受了不得以剥夺国籍把本国的人推给别国的约束。第二年，另两个成员要求发问：多少人失去了国籍，多少孩子没有登记，接下来准备怎么办？
DRP 没有参加开启这一问的表决。它仍可以陈述，并要求陈述完整留在记录里。能说话，与能决定别人不许问，是两种权力。
它的回答是：这是内政，而且法令早于宪约。随后又反问，UCSE，也就是目的联合城邦，自己还要求孩子的父母合法居留满五年，才肯给这些孩子国籍，它有什么资格问？
记录收下了这些回答，也收下了其他成员提供的数字。但 DRP 没有给出被要求说明的人数。这一空白，同样留在记录里。
## 你可以不同意我，不等于我不能问你
如果每一次发问都要先取得被问者同意，那么“我不愿意”就会变成一把永远握在他手里的钥匙。没有上级，本来是为了不让共同机关替成员作主；走到这里，却可能变成谁也不能要求它解释。
所以，订立新约与追问旧事不能用同一把钥匙。前一篇说，新加一项约束，需要相应各方同意；这里问的是，一项已经接受的义务之下，你已经做了什么。
这也不能反过来读成：谁发问，谁就天然有权要求任何国家按他说的答。提出问题的资格，与特定程序中的作答义务，不是一件事。DRP 在这里负有作答义务，是因为它已经接受了宪约中的承诺和程序。没有接受过这份约的体系外国家，不会因为秘书长寄来一封信，就自动负上同样的条约义务。它可以不答；问和不答仍可以公开留下。
被问的一方不握关门权，问的一方也不能独自宣布“你已经答够了”或“你永远答不够”。不然，问便成了另一种发号施令。需要有不由问者独占的认定位置；暂时没有，就如实留下尚未解决的部分。不是每个问题都能立即取得一致的结尾。
回避也不是一句写上去就全都公正。这个故事里的秘书长持 DRP 国籍，因此回避；代行的副秘书长持提问国 NUT，也就是目的民族联盟的国籍。DRP 对此提出异议。秘书处依当时条文认为可以代行，异议仍载入记录。我们可以继续问这条规则是否够好，不必把一次按规则办理写成从此没有偏向。
“这是内政”同样不能把问收走。不替一个国家治理，不等于不许问它怎样治理。那道法令还把失去身份的人留在别国，让出生证上的空白出现在别国的接收中心；它的后果原本就没有停在国界里面。
DRP 对 UCSE 的反问，也不该被当作噪声丢掉。若 UCSE 自己的门槛确实挡住同一批孩子，那就再开一问。可另一方也做错了，不是这一方已经答完了。两个国家可以同时欠同一个孩子一个回答。
记录公开以后，UCSE 删去了父母须合法居留满五年的条件；后来，接收中心出生的孩子中，三百八十九人取得了它的国籍。DRP 也开出新的登记办法，要求父母一方亲自到领事处申请，并补办战时出境手续，到记载的期限内，三十七名孩子完成登记，父母本人的国籍不恢复。
这些变化发生在记录之后，但故事没有证据让我们说，都是那一次追问造成的。改变由各国内部的位置作出，有它们各自的程序。变化可以记，因果不能替它补。两边仍没有解决的部分，也不因“已有进展”而失去名字。
## 如果我的国家不替我问呢
到这里，拿得起话筒的仍是国家。可是，一个人能不能自己把问题递上去，不等外交部门决定他值不值得被代表？
战争中，UCSE 的一次打击命中了邻国的车站候车厅。死者人数，两国公布的数字不同。后来它设立补偿基金，却把资格限于本国公民和境内合法居留的人。二十七户死者家属申请，被挡在外面；另一件事里，三百一十一户农户交过存粮，手里的收据写着战后结算，战后却仍没有结算办法。
家属投诉过，农户申请过。他们不是没有去敲门，而是那几扇门没有给他们一条能走下去的路。这时，三界申诉委员会才变得具体：他们委托律师，自己递交申诉，不靠本国外交部门转交。
委员会没有因此把所有过去的事都接过来。那次打击发生在有关条款生效以前，不在它受理的范围；补偿资格在生效以后仍然把人排除在外，收据也一直没有结算，这些持续下来的问题，它受理了。程序有范围，不等于范围之外的伤害从此不存在。
怎样看这条路是不是真有用？先问三件朴素的事：受不受理由谁定，被问者能不能独自挡住；人实际上递不递得进去；递进去以后，会不会遭报复。委员会由其他委员审议有关 UCSE 的申诉，不由 UCSE 独自定受理。至于故事有没有记载申诉者遭到报复，答案是没有记载。不能把没有记载写成已经查明绝无报复。
委员会随后提出意见。UCSE 后来修改补偿资格，结算收据，也给家属一份删节材料。问确实抵达了作决定的地方。但十九户拿到补偿，还有八户因为死者是否平民无法认定而被拒；农户说按多年前的粮价结算少了三成，材料也没有全部公开。
一个意见不是一场圆满的救济。这个委员会作的是意见，不是判决；成员按事先接受的约作答和落实，不能把它写成拥有法院的全部权力，也不能因此说它什么都没做。该分开写的，是它问到了哪里、改变了哪里，以及哪里还没有人答。
## 那么，共同会议自己呢
如果这条路只能问成员国，不能问共同机关，就会出现一个新的盲点：几个国家单独作决定要回答，凑到一起以后，反而没有谁需要回答了。
沙洲的人逃到石峡邦以后，住进东坪营地。成员会议决定分担转送名额，以户抽签，成年子女单算一户。拒绝抽到的去处，当年就失去转送资格。四十六户人在 NUT 北区有亲属，却抽到别处；其中三十一户拒绝，留在营地。另有九户，成年子女与父母被分到不同国家。
办公室说，抽签分的是名额，不是人，人可以拒绝。这句话不能替实际处境作证。拒绝之后还剩什么，亲人能不能在一起，都要拿出来看。
一部分受影响的人于是申诉共同会议的决定。秘书处认为，这类决定不归申诉委员会管；委员会多数没有接受这份解释，受理了。若秘书处的读法直接成了结论，被问的共同安排就把指向自己的门关上了。
后来，成员会议允许成年子女与父母合为一户，也让拒绝去处的人保留下一年的资格。兄弟姐妹仍不合户。已经失去的那一年，也没有因为新规定便回来。能改，与已经改完，不是一件事。
另一些能提出问题的人，甚至不住在成员国境内。共同措施关闭灰河商货往来时，文件上给人道物资留了例外，实际许可却平均等四十一天，净水药剂还被算作两用物资。对岸诊所与村民也申诉了。若只因他们不属于成员国就不收，措施便可以越过边界影响他们，追问却过不来。
共同会议后来修改了规定，缩短期限，删去净水药剂的限制，安排人道集市。此前诊所断药、商家歇业的那几个月，仍然算数。制定措施的共同程序与负责许可的石峡邦，各须说明自己做了什么，不能互相指过去，让人绕一圈又回到原地。
追问也不能保证通道永远不关。故事后面还有成员退出个人申诉安排，新申诉因此不再受理的事。少掉的那条路是真损失，不能用“仍可在别处发问”轻轻带过；但退出也不能使已经发生的行为、不答的记录和受影响者的问题一并消失。
合作最值得保留的，也许不是大家终于说过同一句话，而是说过以后，仍有人能从出生证、收据、营地和诊所出发，把一句“不对，这里还有事情”送到那些作决定的人面前。
body_en: The child has a birth certificate. In the box for nationality, it says undetermined. Another year passes. The word is still there.

In the source paper’s fictional setting, this is not a clerical omission. During a war, DRP—the Democratic Republic of Purposes—removed the nationality of people who went abroad and failed to return within six months. It would not register their children born abroad. Neighboring countries received the families but maintained their own conditions for citizenship. The parents crossed a border; their children were born between two sets of rules.

Later the three neighbors form a cooperation system. DRP accepts an undertaking not to use deprivation of nationality to push its people onto other states. The following year, its partners ask how many people lost nationality, how many children remain unregistered, and what DRP intends to do. DRP does not vote on opening the question about itself. It may present its account and have that account preserved. Having a voice is different from having the power to prevent anyone else from asking.

DRP answers that nationality is an internal affair and that its decree predates the compact. It also points to UCSE’s own rule: parents must have five years of lawful residence before these children can obtain citizenship there. How, it asks, is UCSE entitled to criticize? The public record includes that response. It also shows that DRP did not supply the requested numbers.
## A question is not a new treaty

Requiring a respondent’s consent before every question would leave a permanent key in the respondent’s hand. The absence of a common superior, intended to prevent takeover, would become a general exemption from explanation. A new obligation and an inquiry into an old undertaking therefore cannot have identical conditions of entry.

The distinction does not give every questioner unlimited authority. Standing to ask and a specific obligation to answer are different. DRP has a duty within this procedure because it accepted the compact’s commitments and process. An outside state does not acquire the same treaty duties merely because the secretary-general sends it a letter. It may decline to answer. The question and the refusal can still remain public.

Nor may the questioner become the sole judge of whether an answer is sufficient. Otherwise questioning turns into command by another route: answer until I, and only I, say you have answered. Closure needs a position the questioner does not monopolize. Where such a position is unavailable, the unresolved part must be recorded as unresolved. An institution need not invent agreement to finish its paperwork.

Recusal is not self-validating, either. The secretary-general holds DRP nationality and steps aside. The deputy taking over holds the nationality of NUT, which initiated the inquiry. DRP objects. The secretariat applies the rule then in force and allows the deputy to act; the objection stays in the record. Following a rule does not make the rule incapable of further criticism.

Calling nationality an internal affair does not remove the question. Asking a government to explain a decision is not taking over its government. Here the decree also has consequences beyond the border: people without nationality live in neighboring countries, and their children’s certificates are issued there. The effects were never wholly internal to begin with.

DRP’s counter-question about UCSE deserves attention, not dismissal as an inconvenient distraction. If UCSE’s residence rule excludes the same children, it too needs an answer. But the second question does not settle the first. Two countries can simultaneously owe explanations to the same child.

After publication of the record, UCSE removes the five-year residence requirement. Eventually 389 children born at its reception center obtain UCSE nationality. DRP introduces a registration route requiring a parent to attend a consulate and regularize wartime departure paperwork. By the recorded deadline, 37 children have been registered through it. Their parents’ nationality is not restored.

These changes follow the record. The case does not establish that the inquiry caused them. They are decisions made by national offices through national procedures. We can preserve the sequence without filling in a causal explanation the evidence does not supply. We must also preserve the people for whom neither change completes an answer.
## If my government does not ask for me
So far, states hold the microphone. What if the people affected could bring a question themselves, without waiting for their foreign ministry to consider them worth representing?

During the war, a UCSE strike hit a station waiting hall in its neighbor’s territory. The countries published different civilian death counts. UCSE later established a compensation fund, but eligibility covered its own citizens and lawful residents within its territory. Twenty-seven bereaved households applied and were excluded. In another part of the case, 311 farming households held receipts for grain taken during the war. The receipts promised postwar settlement. The defense office still had no settlement arrangements.

The families and farmers had tried national routes. The fund rejected the families; the complaints office would not admit their complaints; the defense office said the settlement procedure had not been established. The problem was not that nobody had knocked. The doors offered no usable way forward.

They authorized lawyers to submit petitions directly to the Three-Borders Petitions Committee. Their state later sent a letter supporting them, but their access did not depend on that letter or on diplomatic transmission. That small procedural difference is the difference between having a route and hoping someone else will carry a message.

The committee did not claim jurisdiction over everything. The strike preceded the relevant provision’s entry into force and was not admitted for review. The later application of the compensation law and the continuing failure to settle receipts were admitted. A procedural limit does not erase the earlier harm; it identifies what this particular route can reach.

Three practical questions help test the route. Can the respondent block admission on its own? Can the people actually initiate it? Can they do so without retaliation? Members holding UCSE nationality take no part in examining these petitions, and the committee decides that no usable domestic remedy remains. The case contains no account of retaliation. That is an absence of information, not verification that retaliation never occurred.

The committee issues an opinion. UCSE later changes eligibility, pays for the grain, and supplies an edited document about the strike. Those are changes worth recording. Nineteen households receive compensation. Eight are rejected because the dead person’s civilian status cannot be established. The farmers say payment at the old grain price leaves them thirty percent short. The complete targeting memorandum is not disclosed.

An opinion is not a complete remedy. This committee issues opinions rather than judgments; its members’ duties depend on the undertaking actually accepted. We should neither equip it in the telling with the full powers of a court nor treat its lack of those powers as proof that it has done nothing. The useful account distinguishes what reached the decision-makers, what changed, and what still has no adequate answer.
## And who questions the conference?

A system that can question national governments but cannot itself be questioned creates a curious escape. States must answer separately; together they somehow become nobody’s decision. The shared purpose becomes a place to hide.

People fleeing the Sandbars reach Stonegorge and are housed in Eastfield camp. The members’ conference adopts a plan for sharing transfers. Destinations are assigned by household lottery, with adult children counted as separate households. Refusing the assigned destination means losing that year’s eligibility. Forty-six households with relatives in northern NUT draw other destinations. Thirty-one refuse and remain in camp. In nine households, adult children and parents are assigned to different countries.

The office explains that the lottery distributes places, not people, because everyone may refuse. The sentence does not settle the practical question. What remains after refusal? Can a family stay together? A formally available no may carry consequences that require examination.

Some affected residents petition against the conference’s own decision. The secretariat argues that the petitions provision does not reach such decisions. The committee, by a majority, admits the case. Had the secretariat’s interpretation been conclusive, the common arrangement would have closed the door on a question directed at itself.

The conference subsequently lets adult children and parents count as one household and preserves next year’s eligibility after refusal. Siblings still cannot combine as a household. The year already lost is not returned by the new rule. An arrangement capable of amendment is not an arrangement whose problems have all been amended away.

Some questioners live outside the member states altogether. A common measure suspends commercial traffic at the Grey River crossings while exempting people and humanitarian supplies. In practice, permits average 41 days, and water-purification chemicals are classified as dual-use goods. A clinic and villagers on the outside bank petition too. If membership alone determined who could ask, the measure could cross the border to affect them while their question could not cross back.

The rules are subsequently revised: a shorter permit deadline, removal of the restriction on water-purification chemicals, and a humanitarian market. The earlier months of interrupted medicine and closed businesses still belong in the account. The conference that made the measure and Stonegorge’s office that administered permits must answer for different parts. Neither can send people in a circle by pointing only to the other.

Even these routes are not permanent guarantees. Later in the fictional history, a member withdraws from the individual-petition arrangement and new petitions cease to be admissible. Losing a route is a real loss; saying that questions remain possible elsewhere cannot make it trivial. But withdrawal cannot also erase prior conduct, the record of non-response, or the people still asking.

Perhaps the most valuable thing about an agreement is not that everyone once managed to say the same words. It is that afterward someone can still start from a birth certificate, a receipt, a camp, or a clinic and bring an unfinished question back to the people who made the decision.
